one_liner: Team lead for the Capitol Police vehicle fleet: parts warehouses, inventory, EZ Pass/tags/keys/accident programs, Power BI reporting, budget tracking, and training fleet staff.
fit_summary: The posting requires 52 weeks of specialized experience at the CP-7/GS-9 level in fleet operations, warehouse inventory control, fleet records and expenditure reconciliation, and training fleet personnel, with no education substitution. Daniel's known background is emergency-management consulting at IEM, policy knowledge, and people skills, none of which shows hands-on fleet or warehouse work. Unless Daniel's IEM role directly involved fleet, logistics, or inventory management, Daniel is unlikely to pass minimum qualifications.
eligibility: Open to the public; U.S. citizenship required, so no federal status is needed.

Must show at least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to CP-7/GS-9 covering all four areas: fleet operations analysis, fleet and inventory transactions and reconciliation, warehouse inventory control, and mentoring fleet personnel.
No education substitution: a degree cannot replace the experience requirement.
Must pass a full field background investigation and pre-employment evaluation, then complete a one-year probationary period.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether your IEM work included fleet, vehicle, equipment, warehouse, or supply logistics, such as disaster-response asset tracking. If it did not, consider skipping this posting rather than overstating experience.
If you have relevant logistics work, describe each of the four specialized-experience elements explicitly in your two-page resume, with dates, hours per week, and the systems you used.
Answer the assessment questionnaire truthfully. Only claim 'expert' levels you can back up with a specific resume line, because USCP checks the questionnaire against your resume.
Address the KSAs in the narrative responses as the posting instructs, using concrete examples tied to fleet, inventory, budget tracking, and team training.
Apply well before the extended November 5, 2026 deadline, and save copies of all uploaded documents.
For a better match to Daniel's policy and people strengths, also search USCP and Legislative Branch postings for community outreach, legislative liaison, and emergency-preparedness program roles.
resume_bullets: Tracked and reconciled [number/type] of [vehicles/equipment/supplies] valued at [$ amount] in [system name] for [client/project], updating records and resolving discrepancies [frequency].
Analyzed [logistics/fleet/supply] workflow issues for [client] and recommended [specific change], resulting in [actual result, if known].
Trained and mentored [number] [staff/team members] on [inventory/operational] procedures for [program/deployment] at IEM.
interview_questions: Describe a time you managed inventory across multiple storage locations. How did you keep records accurate?
How have you used Power BI or similar tools to report on operations and spending?
How would you lead and train a team of fleet specialists while making sure project changes stay within the original funding?
Tell us about a time you gathered customer feedback and implemented an improvement.
watch_outs: The specialized experience is narrow and technical, and emergency-management consulting alone likely won't qualify.
The job is fully onsite in Washington, DC, with no telework, which means a daily commute from Manassas.
A full field background investigation and one-year probation are required.
Grade CP-08 has no promotion potential beyond 08.
